requirement.description: The Tags class constructor does not properly validate input types and raises TypeError for invalid arguments like integers, strings, or incorrect parameter combinations. Currently, it accepts various inputs without proper validation, causing the test test_json_tags to fail because it expects a TypeError to be raised.
requirement.contract: The Tags class constructor must validate all inputs and raise TypeError with specific messages when: 1. An integer is passed as a positional argument 2. A string is passed as a positional argument 3. Multiple positional arguments are passed without proper structure 4. A dict with incorrect structure is passed 5. The Tags class should only accept valid tag structures (dicts with Key/Value pairs, Tag objects, AWSHelperFn, or kwargs)

requirement.description: The JobDefinition.validate method does not properly enforce that Tags parameter cannot be a Tags object or Tag object. This leads to the test expecting TypeError to be raised when passing Tags({"foo": "bar"}) as Tags parameter.
requirement.contract: The JobDefinition.validate method must check if Tags property is an instance of Tags or Tag class and raise TypeError with descriptive message if true.

requirement.description: The Table.validate method does not properly enforce that Tags parameter cannot be a simple dict. This leads to the test expecting TypeError to be raised when passing {"Name": "Example"} as Tags parameter.
requirement.contract: The Table.validate method must check if Tags property is a simple dict and raise TypeError with descriptive message if true, ensuring only Tags objects are accepted.
